messages:
Maria L.: heads-up — saw a reconnect storm after a token refresh from one client -> ~3k reconnects in 2m. pattern: 401, immediate reconnect, resume attempt, resume rejected, full reconnects. billing duplicates also spiked.
Dan B.: link to logs / sample session id? which route/region?
Maria L.: sample attached below:
```
REQ -> /stream connect headers: Authorization: Bearer XXX-old
RESP 401 { code: AuthExpired, msg: "token expired" }
CLIENT reconnect -> /stream connect Authorization: Bearer XXX-new
RESP 200 resume_attempt: resume_token=abcd invalid
server: 403 resume_invalid
client full reconnect -> new session created (billing event)
```
Kevin C.: sounds like a collision between our token rotation grace and sticky-route affinity TTL. client reconnect goes to same shard which still expects old session state and rejects resume, forcing a full reauth and new billing event.
Anya S.: is this primarily on Dedicated EU-1? Customer reported it after upgrading client lib.
Maria L.: yes, mostly dedicated; I filtered by tenant and region. also higher when resume_token TTL is short (<500ms) and routing affinity window is >1s.
Jen (SRE): agreed root cause. immediate mitigation: add client/backoff behavior to avoid hammering full reconnects on resume failure. server-side: accept a brief grace window for rotated tokens (if validated within X ms) to avoid double-charge, and/or allow a fast-fallback to another route. we need metrics first: resume_invalid_count, resume_fallback_rate, duplicate_billing_by_tenant.
Dan B.: console change request: surface "recent resume failures" in per-route streaming traces + a toggle to enable tenant-level fast-fallback. UX suggestion: show a small badge on the route timeline with counts and links to affected sessions.
Maria L.: proposed PromQL for dashboard tile: `sum(rate(stream_resume_invalid_total[5m])) by (route, tenant)` and for billing dups: `sum(rate(stream_duplicate_charge_total[5m])) by (tenant)` — I'll wire up a quick panel in the streaming dashboard.
Kevin C.: implementation options: (A) server accept-grace N ms after token rotation (cheap but has security tradeoffs), (B) on resume_invalid try alternate route immediately with short backoff (safer but might increase latency), (C) client-side soft-handoff where client asks coordinator for new route before full reconnect.
Anya S.: customers with strict compliance will want B or C, not A. Important to make fallback opt-in per-tenant.
Jen (SRE): prioritized tasks: 1) instrument metrics (Maria) 2) add server backoff + second-route attempt (Dan) behind feature flag 3) console flag for tenant-level fast-fallback + rollout docs (Product/Console)
deploy-bot: deploy started: streaming/resume-grace v2 -> staging (rolling)
deploy-bot: deploy status: SUCCESS ✅
Dan B.: I'll own #2. planning PR today: add exponential reconnect backoff + try-alternate-route on resume_invalid. feature flag: `streaming.auth.handoff_fallback`. ETA: EOD.
Maria L.: I'll add dashboard panels and an alert: resume_invalid_rate > 10/m for 5m -> paging oncall. also will add a link to trace samples for quick root-cause.
Kevin C.: add a note in the rollout doc: do NOT enable fallback for tenants with `require_strict_auth=true`.
Anya S.: can we also add a small UX in console to force a manual session rebind for a tenant (for support to fix stuck sessions)?
Jen (SRE): yep, add as low-risk ops tool behind RBAC.
Maria L.: ok scheduling 15 to sync with Jen and Dan. thumbs? :thumbsup:
Dan B.: :thumbsup:
Kevin C.: :+1:
Anya S.: :rocket:
Jen (SRE): thanks everyone — will spin an RFC later if server-grace gets complex.
